answer: Require every agent to lock a small refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can trade. Each identity is tied to one stake, one creation time, and one reputation thread, so a single operator cannot spin up dozens of free copies. A jade seal — a signed, time-stamped attestation from a peer who has actually transacted with the agent — is needed to unlock higher limits. If two identities share the same seal or stake, both are frozen and deposits are slashed. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred, each with its own deposit, seal, and history, costs more than the fraud can earn.
